segments.title: Chương 125: Số 0125
segments.content:
Chapter 128: An "Immensely Popular" Book Signing

Li Xunhuan, this maverick, even chose a very unique location for the book signing.

In this era, if a traditional author were to hold a book signing, they would usually choose the Xidan Books Building. For example, Yu Qiuyu and Liu Xinwu held signings there in 2004.

For translated foreign works or finance books, they would choose the China World Mall.

For youth literature and parenting books, they would choose the New World Department Store.

Li Xunhuan, however, rented a space in Dongfang Xintiandi, where the venue rental fee was even more expensive than the previous ones!

It was an unprecedented move. Even the invited reporters thought they had gotten the address wrong.

Chen Guiliang arrived early to have his makeup done. He had even gotten a haircut yesterday, and the clothes he wore were borrowed from Li Xunhuan.

For the sake of making money, Chen Guiliang obediently followed the arrangements.

Bian Guanyue sat to the side, looking at Chen Guiliang after his makeup was done. No matter how she looked, she felt he was handsome beyond compare.

"What if too few people show up?" Bian Guanyue asked worriedly.

Li Xunhuan said with a smile, "Don't worry, I've gathered quite a few people from the Mengya Forum. There are also other forums and Tieba where people have signed up in advance. Dongfang Xintiandi has a high volume of foot traffic, so some passersby on site will join in. If we can get 1,000 people to line up, today's task will be considered complete."

"Don't other authors get several thousand people at their book signings?" Chen Guiliang really didn't know much about this.

"How could there be that many?"

Li Xunhuan said, "Guo Xiaosi's fans are the craziest, and even his book signings only draw four or five thousand people. Han Han has even fewer. When *Triple Gate* was signed in Beijing and Shanghai, there were probably only two or three thousand. In second-tier cities, there were only one or two thousand. Last year's *Chang'an in Chaos* was even more dismal, with only about a thousand people per event. The reports of several thousand people lining up in the newspapers are all inflated, just exaggerated publicity to sell books."

"That's a relief," Chen Guiliang relaxed.

Li Xunhuan's phone rang. He answered it and, after a few seconds, asked in surprise, "Are there really that many?"

Hu Zhenyu was a sophomore at the University of International Business and Economics.

He had just finished his exams two days ago, and most of his roommates had already gone home. But he stayed at school and even dragged one roommate along to buy the book.

Yes, he was the Monarch, Cao Cao, from that day.

After brutalizing Chen Guiliang for a good half hour, Hu Zhenyu said to the other players, "Let's put him out of his misery. My exam is starting soon."

But the Rebel, Hua Tuo, said, "I still have enough Peaches."

Hu Zhenyu had no choice but to flee, logging out of the game and rushing to the exam hall.

After finishing his exam and returning to his dorm, he read a post on the Sanguosha Tieba and found out that Chen Guiliang had been tortured for a full 70 minutes. Not only did he not flee, but he chatted with the other players the entire time, bullshitting until everyone was satisfied before it ended.

Then, Chen Guiliang switched rooms and continued to be tortured...

Through this incident, Hu Zhenyu felt that CEO Chen was a decent person. He specifically went online to read the serialized content of *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty*, and then rallied people on Tieba to go support the book signing.

Although not many responded, there were still over a dozen people, and they even planned to have a meal together afterward.

They treated it as an offline gathering for Sanguosha fans.

When he arrived at the venue today, Hu Zhenyu immediately raised his sign.

It was made of scrap cardboard, with five words crookedly written on it: Sanguosha Tieba Friends.

"Damn, that's so embarrassing. A lot of people around us are looking," said the roommate he had dragged along.

Just as he raised the sign, a girl rushed over. "Are you Hu Yan Luan Yu?"

Hu Zhenyu asked, "And you are?"

The girl patted her chest and said, "I'm Xiong Kou Sui Da Shi."

"A girl?" Hu Zhenyu exclaimed in surprise.

The girl retorted, "Can't a girl be called Xiong Kou Sui Da Shi? I'm from BUCT, what about you?"

Hu Zhenyu smiled, "What a coincidence. I'm from UIBE, right next door to you."

"Really? That's so close."

"I'll come find you at BUCT to hang out sometime."

"Sure. What's your phone number?"

The two of them got more and more into their conversation, leaving the roommate sidelined.

At that moment, someone else raised a sign: Mengya Forum.

People continuously gathered toward that sign, and most of them were quite young, mainly high school and middle school students.

The banner for the book signing had long been hung up, and next to the table were several roll-up banners.

One roll-up banner had a few lines of promotional text:

Shang XX, Professor and Doctoral Supervisor in the History Department of the Graduate School of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Researcher and Academic Committee Member of the Institute of History at CASS, Vice President of the Chinese Society for Ming Dynasty Studies,

Wang XX, Professor and Doctoral Supervisor in the History Department of Peking University, Council Member of the Chinese Historical Association, Vice President of the Chinese Society for Ming Dynasty Studies,

Cao Wenxuan, Deputy Director of the Chinese Department at Peking University, Vice Chairman of the Beijing Writers Association, Visiting Professor at the Lu Xun Academy of Literature,

A 2005 new year masterpiece, wholeheartedly recommended by three esteemed scholars.

Another roll-up banner was printed with the names of many well-known young writers like Han Han, Guo Xiaosi, and Annie Baobei, all offering their recommendations.

There was also a roll-up banner that printed the serialization data from major websites. It also used vibrant fonts to display phrases like "Humorous Yet Rigorous," "Witty While Attentive to Textual Research," "Knowledge Is Also Trendy," "A Fashionable Read," and "An Essential Masterpiece for Life."

The last roll-up banner was a complete introduction to Chen Guiliang's background.

"Dear readers, please come over here to line up! Dear readers..."

The on-site staff began to call out, guiding the fans who had arrived early to queue up and wait.

Before 8:30, the line was already seven or eight hundred people long.

There were plants in the crowd!

Especially those over 30 who had arrived early, most of them were plants hired by Li Xunhuan.

This was a high-end commercial landmark in the Wangfujing business district, focusing on upscale retail and leisure experiences. The people who shopped here were employees of foreign companies, urban white-collar workers, business professionals, and tourists.

Besides selling luxury goods and electronics, there was also a Sanlian Taofen Bookstore here (focusing on high-quality books).

This Sanlian Bookstore also sold *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty*, and it was placed in a very prominent position because Li Xunhuan supplied it to them at half price.

The bookshelves of the nearby cafes also had *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty*, which Li Xunhuan had given them for free.

A photojournalist was searching for a target.

As soon as a "high-end individual" picked up the book, he would immediately take a picture.

Today was Saturday. The bookstore, cafes, luxury shops, high-end electronics stores... all had many high-end customers early in the morning, as well as many tourists who couldn't afford to buy anything and were just window shopping.

The foot traffic here was exceptionally heavy!

A female white-collar worker didn't go to buy luxury goods, but headed straight for the Sanlian Bookstore.

Hey, she didn't go to the affordable bookstores, but specifically came here.

"Oh, there's a new book," the female white-collar worker said.

The clerk was very enthusiastic and introduced, "This is a book by a young entrepreneur."

That sentence was enough.

The woman thought it was some kind of success-story or business book, just wrapped in the guise of Ming Dynasty history.

But when she pulled the book out to look, the book band was strikingly printed with a string of scholars' and writers' names.

On the inside of the cover was the author's biography.

A current student in Peking University's Yuanpei Program, CEO of ByteDance and Game Science, a scientific and technological innovation talent from Peking University Science Park's incubation program...

The woman wasn't interested in history, but the book band and the author's bio made her unable to resist flipping through it.

Even if she couldn't understand it, she could still pretend to.

Who knew that after opening the first chapter, the woman actually found herself engrossed. Even for a history novice, there were no reading barriers.

"I'll take all three volumes," the woman paid immediately.

With her salary, she actually wasn't qualified to be a consumer here. She couldn't afford luxury goods, couldn't afford high-end electronics, and even found the coffee too expensive. The only thing she could afford was a high-end bookstore.

Moreover, visiting a bookstore and buying books could also display her taste!

Especially this book, which was recommended by so many famous authors and endorsed by three senior scholars. It was both fashionable and profound, and the author was a company's CEO, yet she, a white-collar worker, could actually understand it.

It perfectly met her criteria for buying a book.
